### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **68** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-unit.object.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-unit.object.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **18** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c3dfdf6c812906832d556e05082a375b721a7723` — the merge of head `44bf630f1e4704727471be06f8f0e3108c964194` into base `1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c3dfdf6c812906832d556e05082a375b721a7723 && git checkout c3dfdf6c812906832d556e05082a375b721a7723
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880 44bf630f1e4704727471be06f8f0e3108c964194 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880 && git merge --no-ff 44bf630f1e4704727471be06f8f0e3108c964194

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1d7015aeeaa942c37af86c3c93d000fab7024880` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-D) at head `91a494735288e000a7259b2009567ef498473d5d`, read 2026-11-20T09:46Z.

- **One record is owed before landing, with no new head:** a claim amendment (below).
- **One L2 is owed:** CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. It covers the `packages/spec/src/**` face (the new `unitConfig` key, the object door, the ledger rows) and the `Clause-②: yes` declaration. d7-D runs it on this head (7036271727). This ACCEPT does not replace it, and the depth of the write-path design is left to it.

### Owed before landing (a record, not code)

**Amend the claim's file surface.** Claim 7033168211 names spec, objectql, platform-objects, the `organization_admin` rows, the generated spec artefacts, the liveness row and `.changeset/`. The head also edits these ripple files:

- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts` (`unitConfig: 'presentation'`);
- `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts` (`unitConfig: keep`);
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`;
- `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/data.md`;
- the plugin-security integration test.

Each is a classification that a new field key forces, and the body's Ripple paragraph explains it. But other seats' overlap checks read the claim, not the body. Post the amendment and re-run `overlap-check`. No delta L1 is owed.

### Declarations

- **`Clause-②: yes` holds.** It covers the new authorable key and the five new error codes.
- **It is not `(narrowing)`.**
  - The write check runs only for a field that declares the new `unitConfig`, so no stored or accepted shape is refused that was accepted before.
  - The `sys_unit` delete refusal and the explicit `organization_admin` line touch an object that is not released yet: `.changeset/35488-standard-unit-table-sys-unit.md` is still pending on this head. So no released delete narrows.
- **`Metadata-protocol: added`** is right for a new field key.
- **Bumps.** The `minor` bumps follow from it. `@objectstack/spec` is in the `fixed` group, and `platform-objects` `patch` is a docblock.
- **Skills-docs.** The line names follow-up #35808 (folded into #35769). Its absence here is declared: `variant-docs.json` states the gap as `generated-reference-only`.

### Code (L1 read; design depth is the L2's)

- **`unitCodeSources`** reads only `number` + `record` (keyed by `unitField`) and `text` + `code`. A `fixed` quantity stores no code and is checked at parse.
- **`judgedOf`.**
  - Insert judges every source.
  - Update judges membership only when the code or a non-blank quantity is in the payload (Open item 9 point 1).
  - "Required" is a non-blank quantity beside a blank code when either is written (case 3).
  - So a write touching neither is never judged (point 7).
- **`readOrganizationUnits`.**
  - Standard codes are never looked up.
  - It does one read per organization, adding both the exact and the canonical spelling so the hint can be offered, and keys rows by the exact code.
  - An undefined organization asks nothing, so only standard codes pass.
- **`membershipOf`.**
  - Standard first, then the organization's own (retired gives `RETIRED`).
  - A near-miss hint is offered only for a non-retired canonical spelling.
  - `C62` / `EA` point to `H87`.
  - The case-2 message names "a code stored before this write", never the stored value.
- **Engine seams.** The same `assertUnitCodes` runs on insert (after the batch read), by-id update (on the image), predicate update (each prior row with the payload over it) and `validate()` (same condition, refusal recognised by `isUnitCodeRefusal`).
- **Delete refusal.** `refuseOrganizationUnitDelete(object)` runs right after `assertWriteAllowed`, before middleware and hooks, so no context passes.
- **Permissions.** `organization_admin` gets `sys_unit` with `allowDelete: false`, without `modifyAllRecords`, for the reason its comment gives (superuser bits grant delete on their own).

### Tests and controls

- The spec suite: 62 tests.
- The validation suite covers the three Open item 9 cases by name, with the envelope (code and status).
- The engine seams suite includes insertMany culling and the delete refusal under system, user and no context, by id and `multi: true`.
- The real-stack plugin-security suite: 23 tests.
- **Ablations.**
  - Deleting the delete-refusal line reds 3 of 18, and the other-object CONTROL stays green.
  - Short-circuiting the insert `assertUnitCodes` reds 7.
  - Both restores are blob-equal.

### Nits (not owed)

1. **No ablation on the update legs.** The two update hunks, which the body tells a reader to read first, have pins but no ablation. One mutation of the predicate path's `touchesUnitCodes` guard would show those pins are live.
2. **The pending 35488 note goes stale at release.** It says "Nothing reads these tables yet: … the write-time membership check … ship with their own cards", and "organization administrators write it through their existing grant". If both land in the same release, one CHANGELOG would say both that nothing reads `sys_unit` and that the engine now checks codes against it. Correcting that pending note would be a DELIBERATE CORRECTION, which reds `Check Changeset`, and this diff changes code, so the at-tier L2 PASS would have to confirm it. I leave whether to do it to the seat. The 35489 note on its own is accurate.

### Prose, sentence by sentence (changeset)

- **Three modes.** Each one's shape, type restriction and object-door refusals match `UnitConfigSchema` / `refuseDishonestRecordUnitField` as the body lists them and the spec suite pins them.
- **Write check.**
  - "at every insert, by-id update, predicate update and `validate()` preview" matches the four seams.
  - "exact uppercase and of the declared `unitDimension`" and "a quantity may not stand beside a blank code" match `membershipOf` / `judgedOf`.
  - "judged whenever the write touches the quantity or its unit field" matches `judgedOf`.
  - The last sentence ("stays editable in its other fields; a quantity edit beside it is refused") matches case 2.
- **Delete.** "for every caller, a system writer and an automation run included, by id and batched (405 `ERR_UNIT_DELETE_REFUSED`)" is pinned in both suites.
- **Ripple sentence.** It matches the two classifications.

### Gates and routing

- CI at `91a49473`: 62 `success`, 12 `skipped`, none red.
- After the claim amendment and the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS on this head, `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35805` decides the landing route. It reads NOT governed, per d7-D.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `91a494735288e000a7259b2009567ef498473d5d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.ts + packages/objectql/src/validation/unit-code-membership.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-unit.object.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts, packages/spec/liveness/field.json

Inputs read: card #35489 (body and comments 7016814814, 7030061316, 7033168211, 7035276751), PR #35805 (body, 38-file list, net diff from merge-base `b0c624af8c` to the head), the 74 check-runs on the head, ADR-0158 and the Open item 9 settlement 7013996288 the card cites, and the cited code in the tree at the head. Check-runs: every run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending (Test Core 10/10 shards, Type Check, Lint and Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Docs all `success`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Field.unitConfig` is added to the authorable surface** (`data/Field:unitConfig`, JSON Schema `data/UnitConfig`). Right: an additive key with a required discriminator, three closed shapes, matching ADR-0158 L3 (`fixed` needs `unit` and refuses `unitField` and `unitDimension`; `record` needs `unitField` and refuses `unit`) plus Open item 8's `code` marker.
- **Nothing a metadata author could write before is refused now.** `FieldSchema` was already closed, so the bare `unit`, `uom`, `unitCode` and `dimension` keys were refused before; only the message changes. Right.
- **Four new public exports** from `@objectstack/spec`: `UnitConfigSchema`, `UnitConfig`, `UnitConfigParsed`, `standardUnitOf`. Right, and `api-surface/data.json` lists exactly these.
- **Five new wire codes** under `@objectstack/objectql` in the ledger: four at 400, `ERR_UNIT_DELETE_REFUSED` at 405. Right: each is emitted by the module the ledger comment names, and the statuses agree with the thrown classes.
- **New write refusals reach only objects that declare `unitConfig`**, a key that did not exist, so no stored declaration changes meaning. Right.
- **The engine now refuses every delete of `sys_unit`, and `organization_admin` loses the delete bit on it.** A narrowing in form, but `sys_unit` is unreleased (`.changeset/35488-standard-unit-table-sys-unit.md` is still pending in this tree), so no published accept-set shrinks. Right.
- **The object door accepts a `record` pointer into a `text` field that declares a `valueDomain`.** Wrong: see S2.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35489-unit-config.md`: spec, objectql, plugin-security, metadata-core and driver-sql at `minor`, platform-objects at `patch`. This matches what the diff publishes: a new authorable key and new exports (spec), new refusals and exported error classes (objectql), a changed default permission set on an unreleased object (plugin-security), a docblock (platform-objects). metadata-core and driver-sql each gain one classification row for the new key; `minor` is not below what they publish. No major, and none is owed.

`Clause-②: yes`, with `Metadata-protocol: added`, on the PR body and in the changeset body: correct, the change adds to what an author can write and narrows nothing published. `Skills-docs: follow-up #35808` is present. The `Check Changeset` run on the head is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (an organization holding any `sys_unit` row can no longer be deleted): escalated.** The claim holds in the tree: the organization delete refuses while a tenant row outside its cascade names it, and the engine now refuses every unit delete. This follows from Requirement 1 of 7030061316 as written ("every context"), so it is not a defect of this head, but it is a product decision about tenant offboarding and it is the seat's or the maintainer's to rule. It needs a follow-up card filed before this PR merges. The dev's option B (the organization delete's own cascade as the one exemption) is consistent with Open item 11, since a deleted organization cannot re-create a code.
- **Open question 2 (the destructive-change finding for `unitConfig` declared over stored free text): answered A, with a condition.** Settlement point 7 says the refusal's guidance names the backfill door, and this head names none because #35492 has not built it. Shipping the finding and the door's name with #35492 is acceptable only because point 7 ties both cards to one Version Packages release. Nothing in this diff enforces that tie, so the seat must hold the release until #35492 lands; escalated to the seat as a release condition.
- **Out-of-scope note, a `record` pointer declared by an object extension is not judged by the object door: accepted.** Same reach as `currencyField`. The runtime is fail-closed: `unitCodeSources` answers a pointer as written, so a pointer into nothing reads a blank code and the quantity is refused.
- **Out-of-scope notes on the ADR-0158 amendment and the skills teaching: accepted** as the seat's follow-ups (`Skills-docs: follow-up #35808`; no `docs/adr/**` in this diff, as the claim fenced).
- **Deviations: accepted.** The reworded commits keep the tree (`a37e623808`); the files outside the landing zone are one classification row each.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The organization-unit read is one `find` per organization with `organization_id` and `code $in` pushed to the driver, and is skipped when every judged code is standard. The predicate update lays the payload over the matched rows from `readPriorRows`, the memo the currency twin directly above it already reads for the same purpose; the per-row refusal needs each row's id and image. No new in-app join.
- **Cross-organization read: checked, no finding.** The elevated read keeps only the caller's transaction and trace id and names the organization twice; the organization is the row's own, by the same function the home-amount seam uses, and on insert the read runs after the Layer 0 wall's post-hook check.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.ts`.** `standardUnitOf` is an own-property, exact-match lookup, as N4 asks. `toString`, `constructor` and `__proto__` are no members. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`.** One code per remedy, each comment agrees with the emitter. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`.** The union, the type table and the cross-refusals hold against L3 and Open item 8, and the `fixed` enum is built from the same own keys `standardUnitOf` reads.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`.** The five pointer refusals and the shared-field dimension conflict hold against L3. One gap:

S2 (should-fix) — `refuseDishonestRecordUnitField` accepts a `record` pointer whose target `text` field declares a `valueDomain`. L3 says the unit field "carries no marker", and `FieldSchema` already refuses the same pairing on a `code` field. Through the pointer it parses: for example `weight: { type: 'number', unitConfig: { unitMode: 'record', unitField: 'cur' } }` beside `cur: { type: 'text', valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency' }`. One column is then judged as a currency and as a unit, and a quantity write passes only for a coincidental code. The runtime is fail-closed, so nothing wrong is stored, but the accept-set is wider than L3, and closing it after release is a narrowing. Fix: refuse at the door when the target declares `valueDomain`, located at the quantity's `unitField`, with a pin.

**`packages/objectql/src/validation/unit-code-membership.ts`.** The three Open item 9 cases, points 5 and 6, the retired rule (Requirement 2) and the once-per-organization read agree with the settlement. One sentence of its own contract does not hold:

S1 (should-fix) — the module header says "The message prints a code only when the write itself carried it; a resting code is named by its field, never by its value", and the PR body and the proposed ADR note repeat it. Two paths break it for a resting code (case 2, the payload carries the quantity and not the code field):
  - `membershipOf` computes `hint` whether or not the code was written, and the `ERR_UNIT_CODE_UNKNOWN` message prints it. A stored `kgm` or ` KGM` answers "write 'KGM'", which is the stored value in upper case. A stored `ea` or `c62` answers "The piece is 'H87'".
  - the `ERR_UNIT_DIMENSION_MISMATCH` message prints `verdict.dimension`, the dimension of the stored code.
  A caller who may edit the quantity but not read the unit field learns the stored code from the refusal. This is exactly the free-text rows the rollout expects before the backfill. The existing pin covers only the retired path. Fix: when `codeWritten` is false, drop the hint and the stored code's dimension from the message, and pin both paths with `not.toContain`.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts`, `engine-update.ts`, `engine-validate.ts`.** The four call sites sit beside the currency-code check on the same image. The by-id path always has its prior row; the predicate path judges every matched row before the statement; the preview answers the refusal as the row's finding. Holds.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`.** The refusal runs after `resolveObjectName` and `assertWriteAllowed` and before any middleware, hook or driver call. `delete()` is the only engine door that reaches the driver's delete for a business object, so by-id, `multi` and system callers are all covered. Holds against Requirement 1.

**`default-permission-sets.ts`, `sys-unit.object.ts`, `object-schema-fls-references.ts`, `builtin-column-collision.ts`, `liveness/field.json`.** Each agrees with the contract it restates; the liveness row names the real reader.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; fold into the S1/S2 fix or leave):
- N1: the docblock above `STANDARD_UNIT_CODE_LIST` in `field.zod.ts` cites `unit-config.test.ts`; the file is `field-unit-config.test.ts`.
- N2: the `code` beside `valueDomain` message says "no value could satisfy both". `MMK` and `XDR` are both standard units and ISO 4217 codes, and `PR` is both a unit and an ISO 3166 code. The refusal is right; the sentence overstates.
- N3: L3 lists the alias rows for `unitConfig` as one set. Split per variant, some are unanswered: `dimension`, `field` and `codeField` under `fixed`; `defaultUnit`, `unitCode`, `code` and `uom` under `record`. Those get the generic unknown-key answer.
- N4: a whitespace-only code counts as blank, so a standalone `code` field, or a unit field beside a blank quantity, stores `'   '` unjudged.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head and each earns a delta review of its fix.

   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.

  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.

     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
